leverage.exposure: No leveraged position is open right now and the balance is positive. But the recommended move opens one, briefly and by design, and that is the single thing to get right: a buy takes the squad above the floor before the sales bring it back, and a negative balance when the matchday starts scores zero for the entire matchday. Selling Bernardo before bidding cuts the peak exposure to roughly a third, and the window then lasts only from the moment the offer is accepted until the Lokonga sale completes. Do not leave that gap open overnight, and do not place the bid without executing both sales in the same sitting. The second exposure is quieter and easier to miss: the standing Amoako offer becomes a hundred-point penalty the instant the squad reaches eleven players, so pull it as part of this trade.

binding_gap: Not a positional hole - the squad fills a legal formation and can field eleven - but a quality hole at the back. The defence carries two men with no route into a starting eleven at their clubs, so the fielded back line is effectively short of real contributors, and the fifth defender's slot is where the cheapest available points gain sits. Lienhart fills exactly that slot. Beyond it, the constraint is not shape but the eleven-man floor: with only two sales legal against one buy, the funding must come from the two most valuable sellable bodies, and after the trade there is no spare man at all.

verdict.headline: Act.
verdict.detail: Act. After five runs of finding nothing worth buying, the board has produced one: Philipp Lienhart, a Freiburg centre-back who is the only listing verified this run as fit and named in a dated probable XI. Buy him, funded by selling Bernardo and Sambi Lokonga. The reason this clears where every earlier candidate failed is that it is positive on both readings of the same trade - strongly positive if Bernardo is benched as this run's evidence says, and still positive if the previous two runs were right that he starts. It does not require the Bernardo question to be settled. Two hard operational points come with it. Sell Bernardo FIRST, then bid, then sell Lokonga: that order caps the negative-balance exposure at roughly a third of what buying first would open, and if the bid is refused the fallback state is a perfectly healthy squad with cash in hand. And pull the standing Amoako offer before the second sale - it is harmless now and becomes a hundred-point penalty the moment the squad reaches eleven.

sell.reason: Bernardo leads, and he is the one sale that is safe on its own. The freshest Hoffenheim probable XI, read twice this run, has Hranac at left-back and Bernardo out of the eleven entirely - and in the opening match he was substituted off at fifty-three minutes for exactly Hranac, which is a benching rather than a coincidence. Kickbase has carried a doubtful flag on him since the thirty-first. He is not on the league injury table, so this is selection, not fitness. Sell now rather than later: his market value has turned upward, meaning the market has not yet priced the benching, and that edge decays. Selling him alone leaves a legal shape and costs nothing in expected points. Sambi Lokonga is second and strictly conditional - he is the funding leg for Lienhart and nothing else. He is a fit confirmed starter, so this is a complaint about value, not availability: he has the worst points-per-euro in the squad and his value is bleeding. If the Lienhart bid dies, do not sell him; at eleven players that sale is a hundred-point penalty. Amoako is already listed and should stay listed while the squad is twelve. Widmer is NOT a sale - he funds almost nothing and the body insures against the penalty.

He stays on the BLOCKED list on exactly those grounds - do not re-buy him because someone notices he starts. THE COST, STATED HONESTLY: selling him puts AMOAKO into the eleven, and Amoako is a bench man worth ~0, so the swap surrenders his 44 to gain Lienhart's 127. That -44 is already charged inside the +83 expectation in Bzb48ae; it is not a hidden cost. Sell to the board at mv 9.748.111. THE TRAP THAT MUST BE HANDLED IN THE SAME SITTING: Georg has a STANDING OFFER on Amoako at 1.850.000 (ofc 0). It is harmless at 12 players and it is a -100 the instant the squad reaches 11. PULL THE AMOAKO OFFER BEFORE COMPLETING THIS SALE. REVERSAL: he becomes a keeper again if the Lienhart buy dies - in that case close this call, leave him alone, and the squad sits at 11 with 11.156.074 cash and an unchanged expectation.

buy.reason: Lienhart is the whole buy list. Identity was verified two ways this run, which matters because the ledger's own club map had his team wrong: he is at SC Freiburg, not Wolfsburg and not Frankfurt. He started the opening match at centre-back in a four-goal win, came off late with the game already decided, and is named in Freiburg's dated probable XI for the Paderborn game. No injury, suspension or transfer item exists for him since the end of August, and his older injury references are all last-season traps. On price: this is a manager ask carrying a single-digit premium with nobody else bidding on it, so there is no reason to pay a contested premium - bid the top of the measured manager-ask cluster first, and pay the full ask only if that is refused, because the difference is trivial against the points and the trade still ends with a healthy cash cushion either way. A manager ask has no expiry, so the only clocks are tonight's value update and the lock. Everything else on the board was rejected, and the brute-force enumeration is worth stating plainly: higher-scoring end states do exist on raw averages, but every single one of them sells Guirassy - banking a proven elite striker's one-match figure to buy a defender whose one-match figure is nearly double his multi-season mean. That is the regression trap in its worst direction, and it is why those combinations are rejected on expectation rather than on affordability. Castello Jr. is affordable and remains an avoid on the same reasoning, with the added problem that his listing expires inside a few hours and carries no verification from this run.

Per Hntz0sp: ofc 0 means do not pay a contested premium, and the manager-ask cluster is LOW - measured clearings +3,06%, +4,35%, plus this run's Fernandez manager-to-manager at 11.200.000 over mv 10.626.738 = +5,40%. IF HE REFUSES, PAY THE FULL ASK 14.808.555 - the 608.555 difference is trivial against the points and the trade still ends with 6.095.630 cash. There is no listing expiry on a manager ask, so the only clocks are the 20:00Z mv update tonight (a rising mv shrinks the premium on a FIXED ask, so waiting is mildly favourable) and the lock. FUNDING AND THE SEQUENCE, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MUST NOT BE IMPROVISED: sell Bernardo 7.048.552 and Sambi Lokonga 9.748.111 = 16.796.663. End cash at the ask 4.107.522 - 14.808.555 + 16.796.663 = +6.095.630; at 14.200.000 = +6.704.185. DO IT IN THIS ORDER - SELL BERNARDO FIRST, THEN BID, THEN SELL LOKONGA. Selling Bernardo first takes the squad 12 -> 11 = 1/4/4/2 which fills 4-4-2 legally and costs ZERO expected points (he is not starting), and it caps peak negative exposure at -3.652.481 instead of the -10.701.033 you get by buying first. If the bid is then refused, the fallback state is fine: 11 players, 11.156.074 cash, expectation unchanged. THE POINTS. End squad 11 = 1GK/5DEF/3MID/2ATT, 5-3-2, zero spare. Raw MD1 ap: fielded 1395 -> 1416 = +21. On expectation, with Bernardo out of the Hoffenheim XI and Amoako a bench man both worth ~0: 1304 -> 1387 = +83. THE CALL IS THEREFORE ROBUST TO THE BERNARDO QUESTION - it is +83 if he is benched and still +21 if the previous runs were right that he starts. That is why this clears where every prior candidate failed. HONEST CAVEAT: 127 is a ONE-MATCH ap (Hp0rkuf) and so is Lokonga's 44; regressed to plausible multi-season means (~95 for a starting Freiburg CB) the trade is nearer +50. Still the best on the board. BRUTE FORCE CONFIRMS IT: enumerated all 24 unflagged listings x every legal 0/1/2-buy and 0/1/2-sale unwind x all nine formations, keeping only end states with cash >= 0 and >= 11 players. Higher-scoring end states exist on raw ap (Lienhart+Castello selling Bernardo+Guirassy = +146) but every one of them sells GUIRASSY, i.e. banks a proven elite striker's one-match 180 to buy Castello's one-match 199 against a measured 25/26 mean of 106,3 - the exact regression trap Hp0rkuf warns about, in its worst direction.
